claims.claim_vi: The Java Collections Framework is built on interfaces that define basic operations for lists, sets and maps; each data structure is implemented by several concrete classes.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: The Collection interface supports basic operations such as adding, removing and querying elements, and extends Iterable so it can be iterated with the enhanced for-loop or iterators.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Collection has three main subinterfaces: List, Set and Queue.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Collection extends Iterable; List (through SequencedCollection), Set and Queue extend Collection; Map does not extend Collection.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: List is an ordered collection that typically allows duplicate elements; Set contains no duplicate elements; Queue is designed for holding elements prior to processing and typically, but not necessarily, orders them first-in-first-out.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: ArrayList and LinkedList implement List; HashSet and TreeSet implement Set (TreeSet via NavigableSet); PriorityQueue extends AbstractQueue and ArrayDeque implements Deque, which extends Queue.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Implementing Iterable allows an object to be the target of the enhanced for statement.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: In the OpenJDK documentation, the Collection methods that add or remove elements are optional operations: an implementation that does not support one throws UnsupportedOperationException; List.of returns an unmodifiable list whose mutator methods always throw UnsupportedOperationException.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

design_notes_vi: Hình gồm phần gốc (Iterable, Collection), ba nhánh chính kèm ví dụ lớp cài đặt, và nhắc Map nằm ngoài cây. Bỏ các tầng trung gian như SequencedCollection để thấy ba nhánh của nguồn. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source text names no concrete classes (they appear only in its image); the lesson adds ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, TreeSet, PriorityQueue and ArrayDeque, checked against the OpenJDK sources.
Source does not say that Map is outside the Collection tree; the lesson adds it from the OpenJDK Map declaration.

Source describes Collection as supporting adding and removing elements; the lesson adds, from the OpenJDK Collection and List documentation, that adding and removing are optional operations that unmodifiable collections reject with UnsupportedOperationException.
